terms.grammar: dēdō, dēdere, dēdidī, dēditum, reflexive, with dative
evidence: Cic. de Or. 1.57; Arch. 12: hīs studiīs dēditus (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Classical Latin has no verb for “specialize”: it says that one gives oneself up to one pursuit, sē tōtum alicui reī dēdere; dēditus, devoted to it.
A description: to put one’s effort into a single field (see attend).

phrases.latin: Medicus est quī oculīs cūrandīs sē dēdidit.
phrases.english: He’s a doctor who has specialized in treating eyes.

sources: Lewis & Short: dedo · Lewis & Short: opera
